description: Found during defk-ktw, which zeroes alloc/2 in 1 MiB strips with safepoints. Other runtime paths still touch a whole buffer in one call with no safepoint, so a large buffer holds the scheduler there too: defk_copy_T (value-semantics copies, one memcpy), defk_bind's copy of a misaligned input binary (one memcpy at entry), and defk_bits_reserve (memsets the doubled region of a growing bitstring accumulator at once, 32+ MB for a 64 MB output). These need measuring with bench/tick_gap.exs first, then strips where the gap matters.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Runtime paths that copy or clear a whole buffer in one call (value-semantics copies, the aligned copy of a misaligned input, bitstring accumulator growth) work in strips with safepoints, so a large buffer no longer holds the scheduler past a slice

**Current behavior:**
alloc/2 zeroing (defk-ktw) and the range-copy builtins (defk-52v.16) already work in 1 MiB strips charged to the tick budget. Three paths still touch a whole buffer at once, with no safepoint: the value-semantics copy defk_copy_T (one memcpy of the source array), the copy of a misaligned input binary at kernel entry, and defk_bits_reserve (memsets the doubled region of a growing bitstring accumulator, 32+ MB for a 64 MB output). The runtime contract says a kernel yields about every 250 us.

**Desired behavior:**
- First measure each path's scheduler hold with the tick-gap bench (bench/tick_gap.exs, Defk.Bench.TickGap) at sizes where it may exceed a slice (e.g. 8, 64, 256 MB), and record the numbers in docs/performance.md.
- Where the measured gap exceeds the slice, do the work in strips (reuse the existing strip size, tick charging and safepoint pattern) so the gap stays within the contract; where it cannot exceed the slice in practice, record why and leave it.
- The entry copy of a misaligned input happens before the kernel body: if it cannot yield there, say how it is bounded or move it behind a safepoint; resume after a yield mid-copy must continue correctly, and a kill mid-copy frees everything (frames_live back to 0).
- No measurable cost for small buffers (single strip fast path).

**Key interfaces:**
- defk_copy_T, the misaligned-input bind path, defk_bits_reserve in the runtime header; the runtime contract guide if its wording changes

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Tick-gap numbers before/after for each path at the sizes above (provisional if loaded)
- [ ] Tests: large copy, misaligned large input, large bitstring output each yield (yields counter > 0) and give correct results; under forced yields; kill mid-operation leaves frames_live at 0 (test/support/frames.ex helpers)
- [ ] Agreement tests pass; `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- Freeing buffers early (defk-c1e); the max_owned budget

title: Big memcpy/memset at once in the runtime: array copies, misaligned inputs, bitstring growth
